import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clean plot style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc={"axes.edgecolor": ".8", "grid.color": ".9"})

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8), dpi=100)
ax = plt.gca()

# Create a multivariate scatter plot
# X-axis: Price (log scale can be useful for wide ranges, but linear is fine here)
# Y-axis: Megapixels
# Hue: Brand
# Size: Max ISO (reflects sensor sensitivity)
# Style: Body Type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    hue='brand',
    size='max_iso',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(150, 1500),
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.2,
    ax=ax
)

# Add annotations to each point for more context (Model Year and Sensor Type)
for i in range(df.shape[0]):
    row = df.iloc[i]
    ax.text(
        row['price_usd'],
        row['megapixels'] + 1.5,  # Offset text above the point
        f"{row['model_year']}\n{row['sensor_type']}",
        fontdict={'size': 9, 'color': 'black', 'weight': 'semibold'},
        ha='center',
        bbox=dict(facecolor='white', alpha=0.6, edgecolor='none', boxstyle='round,pad=0.2')
    )

# --- Polish the plot for clarity and impact ---

# Set titles and labels
ax.set_title('Camera Feature Comparison: Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=18, weight='bold', pad=25)
ax.set_xlabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)

# Format the x-axis to show dollar values
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.0f')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Adjust axis limits to give points more space
ax.set_ylim(bottom=0, top=df['megapixels'].max() + 10)
ax.set_xlim(left=0, right=df['price_usd'].max() + 500)

# Customize the legend
h, l = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate legends for clarity
legend1 = ax.legend(h[1:4], l[1:4], title='Brand', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left')
ax.add_artist(legend1)
legend2 = ax.legend(h[4:7], l[4:7], title='Max ISO', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.75), loc='upper left')
ax.add_artist(legend2)
legend3 = ax.legend(h[7:], l[7:], title='Body Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.50), loc='upper left')


# Adjust layout to ensure everything fits, including the external legends
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 0.95]) # Make space for title and legend

# Save the final visualization
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
